segments.t: At a Parisian cafe terrace, Gabriel meets actress Virginie Efira while waiting for their director. When the director stands them up, Gabriel decides to reveal an uncomfortable truth about Mathias. Let's listen to the scene in French first.
Il ne vient pas?
Il est où, ton réalisateur?
Il nous a posé un lapin.
Comment ça se passe avec Mathias?
Si tu veux critiquer mon agent, laisse tomber.
De quoi il s'agit?
Tu mérites des gens de ton côté.
Bien sûr. Merci pour le café.
Je vais faire simple. Ramzy te ment.
Mathias aussi. Il te manipule.
Vous n'avez pas touché le même salaire.
Loin de là.
C'est pathétique.
J'ai lu le contrat de Ramzy.
Il y a un autre contrat secret.
Tu veux le voir?
Let's examine how Gabriel reveals Mathias's secret betrayal to Virginie.
Il ne vient pas?
'Is he not coming?' A negative question using the verb venir.
Il est où, ton réalisateur?
'Where is your director?' A familiar question putting the interrogative adverb in final position.
Il nous a posé un lapin.
'He stood us up.' An idiom meaning to stand someone up.
Comment ça se passe avec Mathias?
'How are things going with Mathias?' The reflexive verb se passer asking how things unfold.
Si tu veux critiquer mon agent, laisse tomber.
'If you want to criticize my agent, drop it.' An imperative idiom telling someone to let it go.
De quoi il s'agit?
'What is this about?' An impersonal phrase asking about the subject matter.
Tu mérites des gens de ton côté.
'You deserve people on your side.' The verb meriter expressing what someone is entitled to.
Bien sûr. Merci pour le café.
'Of course. Thanks for the coffee.' A polite formula before leaving.
Je vais faire simple. Ramzy te ment.
'I will keep it simple. Ramzy is lying to you.' The verb mentir in the present tense.
Mathias aussi. Il te manipule.
'Mathias too. He is manipulating you.' The direct object pronoun placed before the verb.
Vous n'avez pas touché le même salaire.
'You did not receive the same fee.' The past tense of toucher meaning to receive money.
Loin de là.
'Far from it.' An adverbial phrase expressing a wide difference.
C'est pathétique.
'This is pathetic.' An evaluative adjective expressing disbelief.
J'ai lu le contrat de Ramzy.
'I read Ramzy's contract.' The compound past tense of the irregular verb lire.
Il y a un autre contrat secret.
'There is another secret contract.' The presentative phrase il y a.
Tu veux le voir?
'Do you want to see it?' The modal verb vouloir followed by the pronoun and infinitive. Now let's listen to the whole discussion again without stopping.

Loin de là.

Gabriel has exposed the secret financial deal behind the film. Virginie now holds the proof of Mathias's betrayal and Ramzy's complicity.
Montre-moi ce contrat.
